findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a part label rather than a hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of GRAPHQL SUBSCRIPTIONS. Most teams reach for GraphQL subscriptions and inherit a broker, a reconnect state machine, and a cache reconciliation problem — to save 2.5 seconds nobody asked for."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the part label to the end: "Most teams reach for GraphQL subscriptions and inherit a broker, a reconnect state machine, and a cache reconciliation problem — to save 2.5 seconds nobody asked for. ... (Part 2 of GRAPHQL SUBSCRIPTIONS.)"

findings.summary: The polling chapter starts on a page titled as a continuation of the client-side chapter, so its own titled page opens in the middle of the section.
findings.evidence: Page 2 is `"page_title":"Client Side: Cache, Reconnect, Gaps (cont.)"` with `"cont":true`, yet it contains `{"type":"heading","text":"Polling Is The Default"}`, "Why Polling Wins", the ETag code block, the decision flowchart and "When To Subscribe"; page 3, titled "When Polling Beats a Subscription", opens with `{"type":"heading","text":"Middle Ground Moves"}`.
findings.fix: End page 2 after the "Strict Mode double-subscribe" callout and move "Polling Is The Default" through "When To Subscribe" onto page 3 under the "When Polling Beats a Subscription" title, pushing "Middle Ground Moves" and the decision table to a page 4 marked `(cont.)`.

findings.summary: The decision flowchart's hybrid branch names two patterns that are only explained on the following page.
findings.evidence: Page 2 flowchart nodes `"c2_0":{"text":"notify then fetch"}` and `"c2_1":{"text":"smart intervals"}`; page 3 first defines them: "Smart polling: fast when focused, slow when backgrounded" and "Notify-then-fetch: event says 'changed', client refetches cached query".
findings.fix: Place the flowchart after the "Middle Ground Moves" bullets (i.e. on the page that defines smart polling and notify-then-fetch), or add a one-line gloss to each hybrid node so it stands alone where it currently sits.

findings.summary: The "arithmetic" callout's first rule tells readers to poll for rare events, contradicting the handbook's own "rare but urgent → subscribe" guidance on page 2 and its flowchart.
findings.evidence: Page 3 callout: "If time between events is greater than the poll interval, poll." Page 2: "Irregular but urgent: an alert, a finished long job / Polling burns requests waiting on a moment that may never come", and the flowchart routes "rare but urgent" to the "subscribe" branch.
findings.fix: Qualify the rule with the freshness condition that the rest of the part uses, e.g. "If time between events is greater than the poll interval AND a delay of one poll interval is acceptable, poll; if the event is rare but must arrive within seconds, subscribe or notify-then-fetch."

findings.summary: Chapter-10 gotchas material is placed on the polling page, so the page titled "Gotchas, Testing, Decision Summary" begins after the gotchas have already started.
findings.evidence: Page 3 (`"page_title":"When Polling Beats a Subscription"`) contains `{"type":"heading","text":"Publish After Commit"}` and `{"type":"heading","text":"Silent Failures"}`, while page 4 (`"page_title":"Gotchas, Testing, Decision Summary"`) opens with `{"type":"heading","text":"Load Multipliers"}` — a continuation of the same gotcha list.
findings.fix: Move "Publish After Commit" and "Silent Failures" to the top of the "Gotchas, Testing, Decision Summary" page (splitting it into two pages with `cont:true` if it overflows), leaving the polling page to end on the honest-cost table.

findings.summary: The claim that deletion requires manually filtering every cached list is wrong for Apollo's InMemoryCache, which filters dangling references out of list fields automatically on read.
findings.evidence: "Deletion must evict the entity AND filter every cached list" — Apollo's docs state that after `cache.evict`, "dangling references will be automatically filtered from lists whenever those lists are read from the cache" (array fields without a custom `read` function get an implicit `.filter(canRead)`).
findings.fix: Reword to: "Deletion evicts the entity; Apollo auto-filters dangling refs out of plain list fields on read, but you must still fix single-reference fields, counts/pagination metadata, and any list with a custom `read` function."

findings.summary: The two hardest cache operations — insertion and deletion — are asserted with no example, while easier points on the same page and the next get code blocks.
findings.evidence: "A new list item needs `updateQuery` or a cache modifier" and "Deletion must evict the entity AND filter every cached list" appear as bare bullets, whereas the split link and the `304 Not Modified` poll each get a `{"type":"code"}` block.
findings.fix: Add a short code block showing both, e.g. `cache.modify({fields:{messages:(refs,{toReference})=>[...refs, toReference(newMsg)]}})` for the addition and `cache.evict({id})` followed by `cache.gc()` for the removal.

findings.summary: The decision flowchart's arrows run from the recommendation to its criteria, inverting the direction a learner reads a decision tree in.
findings.evidence: `{"from":"n0","to":"b0"}` (freshness need → poll) followed by `{"from":"b0","to":"c0_0"}` (poll → "low update rate") and `{"from":"b1","to":"c1_0"}` (subscribe → "sub-second, high rate").
findings.fix: Reverse the second level so conditions feed decisions — `low update rate` → `poll`, `sub-second, high rate` → `subscribe` — or relabel the leaf nodes as outcomes ("use when: update rate is low") to make them read as justifications rather than consequences.

findings.summary: The k6 command sets `--vus` with no duration/iterations, which on k6 releases before v2.1.0 makes the flag ignored so the "5000 connection" load test silently runs one VU.
findings.evidence: "k6 run --vus 5000 subscribe.js  # ws module" — k6 warns "the `vus=5000` option will be ignored, it only works in conjunction with `iterations`, `duration`, or `stages`"; only k6 v2.1.0 changed `--vus` alone into a shared-iterations shortcut (5000 VUs, 5000 total iterations).
findings.fix: Write `k6 run --vus 5000 --duration 10m subscribe.js` so the ramp is version-independent and the connections are actually held open.

findings.summary: The summary decision table mixes dimension names and applicability conditions in the same column, so the rows cannot be read consistently.
findings.evidence: `"headers":["Choose","Default","Escalate to"]` with rows `["transport","SSE","WebSocket if duplex"]`, `["legacy only","long poll","nothing"]`, `["backend","Redis, ephemeral UI","Kafka or JetStream"]`, `["dev only","in-memory","anything real"]` — "legacy only" and "dev only" are conditions, not things being chosen.
findings.fix: Keep one row per dimension and fold the caveats into the cells: `["transport","SSE","WebSocket if duplex; long poll only for legacy"]` and `["backend","Redis for ephemeral UI (in-memory is dev-only)","Kafka or JetStream when durable"]`.
